Marathon Petroleum has climbed nearly 12% over the past week, with today's modest gain continuing a sharp recovery from lows hit on November 6th. The rally coincides with refinery utilization hitting 95.2%—near operational capacity—and heating oil prices surging 59% year-over-year, which boosts demand and margins for refiners who produce these products. Rising crude prices (US oil at $89.62/barrel, up from recent lows) combined with tight product inventories creates favorable conditions for refining profits.

However, the broader oil market backdrop is turning less supportive. Russia's crude production has bounced back following Trump administration diesel negotiations, and global supply has shifted into surplus according to the IEA, which typically pressures crude prices lower over time. This supply recovery could crimp the refining margins that have driven the stock's recent strength.
